task 3: plan-defect: M2/M3 spell `kata.patchMetadata(projectId, task.uid, patch)` with three arguments, but `fleet/kata-client.mjs`'s signature is `(projectId, uid, patch, revision)` and sends `If-Match: "rev-<revision>"` — a 3-arg call against a live hub sends `"rev-undefined"` and takes a 412. Implemented as written (that is also what the exam measures); the engine (task 5) must hand `factoryTools` a kata whose `patchMetadata` fills the revision it tracks, exactly as `fleet/janitor.mjs:229` already wraps it with `metadataPatch(transport)`. A wiring note for the engine, not a defect in this module — the leg is satisfiable as specified.

task 3: `factory/` is `fleet/`'s sibling and there is no repo-root `node_modules`, so a bare import of `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` from `factory/tools.mjs` does not reach `fleet/node_modules` — node's upward walk skips it. The module climbs three rungs (bare specifier, the package's declared entry read off `fleet/node_modules/<spec>/package.json`, then `require.resolve` anchored at `fleet/package.json`). Exam legs (a)-(d) still need sibling task 1's dependency actually installed in the fold tree; nothing was installed at BASE, so those legs were verified here against an offline stand-in for `createSdkMcpServer`/`tool`/`z` rather than the real SDK.

task 3: The returned config also carries the `tool()` definition array as `config.tools`, so leg (a)'s alternative reading ('invoking the config's tool handlers exported for the exam') has a handle that needs no MCP client; the SDK's own `instance` registration is unchanged.

task 1: plan-defect: the dependency line is declared in fleet/package.json while the only consumer is factory/worker.mjs, and Node resolves a bare specifier from the importing file's directory upwards — it never reaches fleet/node_modules. Fixed task-locally inside worker.mjs: the lazy load tries the bare specifier first, then resolves the package from fleet/package.json by hand (createRequire + pathToFileURL). Verified the default path reaches the real CLI (it fails on auth in this sandbox, which is expected). If a later task moves the dependency to a root manifest, that second try becomes dead code and can go.

task 1: amendment (clause): M2 says the options carry settingSources, permissionMode, cwd, systemPrompt, model and disallowedTools and that mcpServers is passed through when given; I read maxTurns and maxBudgetUsd the same way — present in the options exactly when the dispatch named them — since the call shape in Context lists them as options of the dispatch and the clause never says where else they would go. — The clause enumerates what must be present without saying what happens to the two budget options the same call shape declares; omitting them would have made them unreachable for every caller, and emitting them as undefined would override the SDK's own defaults.

task 1: amendment (clause): The Context sentence 'deps is the second argument and defaults to { query } from the SDK' is implemented as a lazy dynamic import in a try/catch at module load, not a static import, and interruptWorker resolves undefined for a handle with no interrupt() rather than throwing. — A static import would make factory/worker.mjs unparseable in a tree with no install, which is exactly the tree the exam runs in (it drives a fake deps.query and never needs the package). A supervisor that races a worker which already finished is not itself an error.

A re-run of the exam in THIS clone stays green, but a fresh checkout of the branch, or a clone without `fleet/node_modules`, puts the exam straight back to `Cannot find package '@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk'`. The durable answer is sibling task 1 (#81fw) declaring the SDK in `fleet/package.json` plus whatever install step the fold runs before the suite; nothing inside this task's FILES can carry it. I chose to provision rather than return BLOCKED because provisioning actually measures the module against the peer's exam, which BLOCKED would not have.

It forbids any diff under fleet/, while M5, Proof Run #2 (`node -e "...require('./fleet/package.json')...dependencies['@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk']"`), exam leg (f), and the task's own `Modify:`/FILES: lines all require fleet/package.json to gain that dependency line, which BASE does not have. Separately, the driver's own exam handoff lands at fleet/tests/exams/run_184/test_factory_worker.mjs, so the check is red on the handoff alone, before any implementer edit — and since every task in this plan owns a fleet/tests/test_factory_*.mjs file, this will red for all five tasks. Suggested narrowing: `git diff --quiet $ULTRA_BASE -- fleet/ ':(exclude)fleet/package.json' ':(exclude)fleet/tests'`.

task 2: amendment (clause): M1's "each pair question built from `sets.landing.pairwise` with `<i>` and `<j>` substituted": `<i>` substitutes to the clause number (i+1) in `pairwise.key` and to the zero-based array index (i) in `pairwise.instructions`, so the first clause's pair over file f0 is keyed `M1__f0` and asks about `clauses[0]`. — A single substitution base cannot satisfy leg (a), which requires the key `M2__f1` and that same question to contain `clauses[1]`. The two spellings are the template's own — factory/proto/loop.mjs builds `M${i+1}__f${j}` with question text `clauses[${i}]`, and questions.json names that prototype as this set's provenance — so the key cites the Machine clause as the task text numbers it while the question cites the state subscript the reader indexes.

task 2: amendment (clause): M4's "answers without a key the reader needs": a reply carrying none of the answers a reader reads is the null-plus-one-line lane (so an `{}` reply refuses on all six readers, per leg (f)), but a reply carrying some of them is read from what is present — a missing answer simply does not fire its gate, so gradeFinding needs affirmative evidence to reach 'blocking' and readTask opens neither k nor the referee on an answer that never came. readLanding alone additionally requires `claim_established` and at least one pair answer per clause. — Leg (e) names a different subset of the task answers in each sub-case (the first three vary difficulty and design_open, the last two review_difficulty and doc_or_prose_only), and leg (b)'s blocking vector names six of the ten landing questions. Requiring every asked key would turn a partial fake into a null and make those legs unsatisfiable, while the conservative reading keeps the gates evidence-driven: no answer, no promotion.
